name: Runner
subtitle: Continuously moving forward while managing path, obstacles, and rhythm; core is readability and choice cost.
demoRuleHint: Rule: Auto-forward (base 5 m/s) → Obstacle/branch appears → Input (slide/jump/turn) → Judgment (pass/fail) → Speed/combo changes
problemsSolved: Use minimal input to create multiple branching choices (lane/jump/turn/branch).
Standardize obstacle readability and advance notice, reducing "can't see, then die".
Use speed and segment structure to create rhythmic peaks and troughs, avoiding monotonous straight lines.
learningGoals: Understand how path branching creates decision density.
Master how speed, camera, and readability affect difficulty.
Be able to design levels with "low input cost but high decision value".
minimalRules: Forward speed: base 5 m/s, combo bonus +0.5 m/s per combo, max 8 m/s.

Obstacle judgement: jump pass requires triggering jump within 0.3 s before obstacle, jump height ≥1.2 m; slide pass requires sliding within 0.2 s before obstacle; turn pass requires completing turn when lane spacing ≥1.5 m.
Reward system: collecting items increases combo +1; combo ≥5 triggers combo bonus 1.2× speed; combo lasts 10 s.
systemLoopHint: Input (jump/slide/turn) → Judgment (pass?) → Feedback (speed/combo) → Scene progression → New obstacle → New input

combos.effect: Earn 1 experience point every 10 m; upon reaching 5 points, unlock a new running stance or item, raising the maximum combo cap.
Collect energy items to trigger abilities (e.g., sprint, shield); ability charge accumulates from combos, and combos reset after use.
Procedurally stitch track segments; obstacle types and density are randomly generated along a difficulty curve, maintaining player adaptability.

advancedWarnings: Insufficient readability leads to "reaction failure" rather than "decision failure", causing players to lose rhythm.
Too high obstacle density overwhelms choices, turning the game into pure reaction and reducing depth.
Too low obstacle advance time can actually increase rhythm, but also raises misjudgement rates because players must decide faster, leading to over-anticipation and delayed reaction.
advancedAlgoRefs: Level: segment stitching, difficulty rhythm arrangement.
Judgement: terrain collision, jump trajectory, camera follow.
